definition: Move the stop to a fixed level beyond entry as the profit passes each step: above trigger_1 the stop locks lock_1 of the entry price in profit, above trigger_2 lock_2, above trigger_3 lock_3; the highest step passed wins and the stop never moves back.
boundaries: Before the first step the level is missing and the unit's own initial stop holds. The profit is read at the bar's high for a long and its low for a short, as freqtrade's backtest reads it. Which exits and halts a unit may use, and their numbers, are the risk session's call (ledger R-04); this entry says what the rule does, not whether to use it. QML's unit runtime does not yet pass an exit its position, so inside a unit this exit stays silent until it does. One instance serves one position at a time on its side, and the entry price names the position: an entry price other than the one it holds starts a new position with fresh state. Two positions back to back at the very same entry price would share state until the runtime names each position.
recognition: Each time the trade reaches a profit step the stop jumps up to lock more in.

class_meanings.perp: freqtrade scales a futures trade's profit ratio by its leverage; this ratio is the price's, before leverage.
class_meanings.index_cfd: a gap across the close moves past the level between two bars; the exit reads the next bar.
